model.name: Position
model.purpose: Govern an organizational Position as a reusable slot of work that exists independently of any occupant: identity, official designation, classification, hosting unit, reporting, duties and authorities, establishment and vacancy, lifecycle, location, requirements, pay-band constraints, evidence and interoperability. Occupancy of the slot is composed through assignment rather than stored as the Position itself.
model.scope_statement: This model covers a Position (also called a post in civic and W3C ORG usage, and a classified job-slot in public-service HR) as the work consisting of duties and responsibilities assignable to an employee or other holder, which may be vacant, abolished, geographically bounded, or held by more than one person. It does not own the person, the occupancy interval, the team, the unit hierarchy, the occupation taxonomy, or the recruitment advertisement; those are sibling or aligned models.
in_scope: Canonical identity, official and alternate titles, and notation of a Position or post that exists independently of any current holder.
Hosting organization or organizational unit, reporting relationships between posts, and binding of a Position to an abstract role or function.
Classification of the Position into class, series, grade, pay plan or equivalent job-evaluation outcome.
Alignment of the Position to an occupation or job-kind taxonomy such as ISCO-08, O*NET-SOC or a local scheme, without owning that taxonomy.
Duties, responsibilities, authorities, supervisory relationships and qualification requirements assigned to the Position.
Establishment, authorized full-time-equivalent capacity, vacancy, abolishment, reclassification and other Position-level lifecycle states.
Duty station, site and, where relevant, geographic area or constituency associated with the Position.
Position-level remuneration band or salary range, distinct from an occupant’s actual pay.
Position description and classification-evaluation artifacts, certification, access, retention and interoperability profiles.
out_of_scope: The Person, Practitioner or other Agent who may occupy the Position; occupant identity belongs in a person model.
The occupancy, membership, employment or assignment interval that binds a person to a Position (WM-ORG-016 and org:Membership / schema.org EmployeeRole).
Organizational unit hierarchy, legal entity and team membership as first-class structures (WM-ORG-002, WM-ORG-003), except the hosting and reporting links from this Position.
Occupation, competency, qualification and skills taxonomies as master data (ISCO, ESCO, O*NET, local role catalogues); this model only stores alignments.
JobPosting, requisition campaign, candidate and recruiting-process records, except the fact that a vacancy is authorized against a Position.
Individual compensation, payroll, benefits, time and attendance, and performance appraisal of an occupant.
Financial-instrument, accounting, geospatial-coordinate and sports-playing senses of the word position.
Military rank as a personal status, academic degree, and professional licence as person properties; the Position may require them but does not own them.

boundary_notes.distinction: A unit contains or governs Positions (org:hasPost / org:postIn). The unit is the structural container; the Position is the work-slot inside it and must not duplicate unit hierarchy, purpose or legal identity.
A team is composed through Positions and assignments. Positions remain reusable slots; team membership of people is not stored on the Position.

W3C ORG allows org:holds / org:heldBy directly on a Post; Popolo forbids those properties and requires occupancy through Membership. This model treats occupancy as a composed assignment so that vacant, historical and multi-holder cases remain representable without collapsing person into Position.

A role is a reusable function (for example CEO or Member of Parliament) that many Positions can share. A Position is the organization-specific slot (CEO at a named body; MP for Avalon). Role taxonomies are aligned, not owned.

ISCO defines a job as a set of tasks performed or meant to be performed by one person, and an occupation as a set of similar jobs. Occupation is a statistical and labour-market kind; Position is an established slot in a named organization. Occupational codes are alignments on the Position.

EmployeeRole describes an employment relationship with startDate, endDate and baseSalary of a person. JobPosting is a public listing of an opening. Neither is the standing Position; a posting may be authorized against a vacant Position.

PractitionerRole is typically the set of roles, locations and services a named practitioner performs for an organization during a period. It may be used with an empty practitioner for an un-named slot, but its default semantics are occupancy-plus-service rather than a classified HR Position. Align, do not equate.

Holdings, coordinates and playing-position uses are outside this organizational work-slot model. schema.org Role.roleName even cites Quarterback as a namedPosition, which must not be treated as WM-ORG-004.

sources.title: The Organization Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative org:Post, org:Role, org:Membership, org:holds/heldBy, org:postIn/hasPost, org:reportsTo, org:remuneration and ChangeEvent semantics for a position that exists independently of its holder.

sources.title: Popolo Post data specification
sources.relevance: Civic Post as a position independent of its holder; distinguishes post from role; requires organization; records creation and elimination dates, geographic area, contact and labels; rejects direct org:holds occupancy.

sources.title: 5 U.S. Code § 5102 - Definitions; application
sources.organization: United States Congress / Legal Information Institute
sources.relevance: Statutory definition of position as the work consisting of the duties and responsibilities assignable to an employee, plus class of positions and grade, with enumerated exclusions (unpaid, fee-basis, seasonal, experts, trades and others).

sources.title: 5 CFR 511.101 Definitions (Classification Under the General Schedule)
sources.organization: U.S. Office of Personnel Management / National Archives Office of the Federal Register
sources.version_or_date: 5 CFR Part 511 Subpart A, eCFR current as of 2026-08-20
sources.relevance: Regulatory definition: Position means the work, consisting of the duties and responsibilities, assigned by competent authority for performance by an employee; plus class, grade and classification.

sources.title: Introduction to the Position Classification Standards
sources.version_or_date: TS-134 July 1995, TS-107 August 1991, revised August 2009
sources.relevance: Federal definition of Position and Position Description; official titles; classification of work; requirement that the PD be kept current and certified by the immediate supervisor.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Resource PractitionerRole
sources.relevance: Period-bounded role at an organization and location, identifiers, active flag, empty-practitioner unnamed-slot pattern, specialty, location and healthcareService; boundary with CareTeam and Practitioner qualifications.

sources.title: schema.org Occupation
sources.relevance: Occupation as a profession with occupationalCategory (O*NET-SOC, ISCO-08), education and qualification requirements, responsibilities, skills, estimatedSalary and occupationLocation; used on JobPosting and Person.hasOccupation, not as an org-specific slot.

sources.title: International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO-08)
sources.version_or_date: ISCO-08, adopted December 2007 and endorsed by the ILO Governing Body March 2008
sources.relevance: Normative job versus occupation versus skill definitions; four-level structure used to classify jobs worldwide, including Armed Forces Occupations as Major Group 0.

sources.title: ISO 30400:2022 Human resource management — Vocabulary
sources.relevance: ISO/TC 260 HR vocabulary covering organization, workforce composition, workforce planning and allocation, recruitment and related terms. Exact published definitions of job, role and position were not inspectable in full text during this run and must not be treated as quoted.

sources.title: schema.org EmployeeRole
sources.relevance: Employee relationship with baseSalary, salaryCurrency, startDate, endDate and roleName; numberedPosition on OrganizationRole. Distinguishes occupancy-pay from the standing Position and shows sports namedPosition as a conflicting sense.

sources.title: Popolo Membership data specification
sources.relevance: Occupancy of a Post occurs through Membership with start and end dates, optional post, role, on-behalf-of organization and geographic area; used to bound WM-ORG-016 against this Position model.

sources.title: HRDG 4511 Section B - Position Descriptions
sources.organization: USDA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service
sources.version_or_date: APHIS HRDG 4511 Section B, page dated 2020-06-02
sources.relevance: Operational definition of the Position Description as the official record of management’s assignment of duties, responsibilities and supervisory relationships; legal basis for appointment, pay, qualifications, selection and performance plans.

bundles.name: Identity and designation
bundles.description: How a Position is uniquely identified, officially titled, labelled and distinguished from nearby slots in the same organization.
bundles.rationale: W3C ORG, Popolo and US classification all treat a post or position as a named, identifiable resource whose official title is not the same thing as a date, a person name or an occupation code.

layers.name: Canonical identity
layers.description: Master identifiers, IRIs and local keys for the Position as a first-class entity.

findings.name: Position identifiers
findings.description: A Position needs at least one stable identifier from the authoritative HR or organization register, optionally a governed IRI, and a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID when the master system does not supply a durable key. Dates of creation are not identifiers.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier for this Position, and which system issues and guarantees it?
What governed global IRI, if any, identifies this Position, and what UUID or ULID has the adopting Dimension assigned?
Which additional business identifiers (HRIS position number, budget line, FHIR PractitionerRole.identifier, org:identifier notation) apply, and how do their schemes differ?
How are duplicate or merged Position records detected and which identifier remains canonical after a reorganization?

data_elements.name: Master position identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the authoritative HRIS, classification or public-organization register.

data_elements.name: Position IRI
data_elements.description: Governed HTTP IRI for the Post or Position when published as linked data.

data_elements.name: Dimension UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Adopting-Dimension identifier used when no durable master key exists or as a cross-system correlation key.

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme
data_elements.description: Datatype, CodeSystem or register that distinguishes the notation scheme, consistent with org:identifier as a skos:notation specialization.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identifiers and scheme metadata are reference data on the Position record; they are not a separate serial artifact unless an identity-resolution log is later attached.

layers.name: Titles and labels
layers.description: Official title, preferred label, alternate labels and local working names.

findings.name: Official title and labels
findings.description: US classification requires authorized official position titles for HR, budget and fiscal purposes. Popolo and ORG use skos:prefLabel and skos:altLabel. Working titles must be distinguished from the official title.

questions.text: What is the official or preferred title of this Position, in which language, and is it drawn from an authorized title list?
What alternate labels, abbreviations or working titles are in use, and which audiences may use them?
Does the official title include a required supervisory, leader or honorary prefix or suffix, and under what rule was it applied?
Who has authority to change the official title, and is a reclassification required before the change takes effect?

data_elements.name: Official title
data_elements.description: Authorized or preferred label of the Position.

data_elements.name: Alternate labels
data_elements.description: Abbreviations, historical titles and informal names.

data_elements.name: Working title
data_elements.description: Local name used in the organization that is not the official classified title.

data_elements.name: Title language
data_elements.description: BCP 47 language tag for each lexical label.

artifacts.name: Authorized title record
artifacts.description: Evidence of the official title assignment, including any required prefix or suffix.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master position identifier plus title-version serial; do not use the title string as the identifier.

bundles.name: Classification and occupational alignment
bundles.description: How the Position is classed for pay and personnel administration, and how it is aligned to labour-market occupation taxonomies without owning those taxonomies.
bundles.rationale: US law defines class and grade from similarity of work, difficulty and qualifications. ISCO classifies jobs into occupations by skill level and specialization. schema.org occupationalCategory points at ISCO-08 and O*NET-SOC. These are alignments on a Position, not the Position itself.

layers.name: Class, series and grade
layers.description: Local job-evaluation outcome: occupational series, class of positions, grade or band, pay plan and classification status.

findings.name: Position class and grade
findings.description: A class of positions groups work that is similar in kind, difficulty and qualification requirements. A grade groups classes equivalent in difficulty and qualification level for one range of basic pay. Classification is the analysis that places a Position in a class.

questions.text: What occupational series, class, grade or pay band is assigned to this Position, under which pay plan or job-evaluation scheme?
Is the current classification certified, draft, under appeal, or superseded, and who classified it?
Which classification standard, flysheet or job-family standard was applied, and does the Position fall outside that standard’s coverage?
Is the Position classified as supervisory or leader, and which factor or guide produced that determination?

data_elements.name: Pay plan code
data_elements.description: Local pay system identifier such as General Schedule, Federal Wage System, or a non-US analogue.

data_elements.name: Occupational series
data_elements.description: Series or family code in the local classification scheme.

data_elements.name: Grade or band
data_elements.description: Grade, band or level used for a range of basic pay.

data_elements.name: Classification status
data_elements.description: Certified, draft, appealed, superseded or not-applicable-to-this-regime.

artifacts.name: Classification evaluation statement
artifacts.description: Record of the analysis that assigned series, title and grade, including factor evaluation where used.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Classifier-office evaluation identifier plus Position master id; versioned on each reclassification.

layers.name: Occupational taxonomy alignment
layers.description: Mapping of the Position’s work to ISCO-08, O*NET-SOC or another occupation codebook.

findings.name: Occupation code alignment
findings.description: ISCO defines a job as a set of tasks and duties performed or meant to be performed by one person, and an occupation as a set of similar jobs. A Position is typically one established job-slot and should carry zero or more occupationalCategory alignments with explicit codebook identity.

questions.text: Which occupation codes from which code sets (ISCO-08, O*NET-SOC or other) describe this Position, including code value, label and codebook version?
Is each occupational mapping exact, broader, narrower or related, and what evidence supports it?
If the Position is a military job-slot, is it aligned to ISCO Major Group 0 Armed Forces Occupations rather than a civilian group, and is rank still excluded as person status?
What ISCO skill level, if any, is implied by the mapped unit group, and how does it relate to local qualification requirements?

data_elements.name: Occupational category
data_elements.description: Coded occupation with codebook identity, repeating for each applicable value.

data_elements.name: Mapping relation
data_elements.description: Exact, broader, narrower or related correspondence to the codebook concept.

data_elements.name: ISCO skill level
data_elements.description: Skill level 1 to 4 associated with the mapped major or unit group.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Occupation codes are reference alignments to external classifiers; the codebook itself is not an artifact of this Position.

bundles.name: Structural placement and relationships
bundles.description: Where the Position sits in an organization, whom it reports to, which abstract role it plays, and how it composes teams without absorbing unit or person models.
bundles.rationale: ORG and Popolo require a Post to exist in an Organization. Reporting can be post-to-post independently of incumbents. Role is a function the holder plays. Teams and assignments are composed, not duplicated.

layers.name: Host organization and unit
layers.description: The organization and unit in which the Position is established.

findings.name: Hosting organization and unit
findings.description: Popolo requires every Post to assign organization or organization_id. ORG provides org:postIn / org:hasPost. The Position must not restated the unit’s own hierarchy.

questions.text: In which organization and organizational unit is this Position established, and are those references to WM-ORG-002 instances?
Is there any permitted exception to the rule that a Position cannot exist outside an organization?
Does holding this Position confer ex officio membership of another body, and which body is that?
Is this Post also treated as an Organization (for example a committee or timeshared post held by a group), and if so how is that dual typing governed?

data_elements.name: Host organization reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the organization in which the Position exists (org:postIn).

data_elements.name: Host unit reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the organizational unit that contains or governs the Position.

data_elements.name: Ex officio links
data_elements.description: Other bodies the holder joins by virtue of this Position rather than as an individual.

data_elements.name: Post treated as organization
data_elements.description: True when the Post is also modelled as an Organization, as ORG permits for multi-holder or committee posts.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Hosting and ex officio links are typed references to sibling organization and unit records, not standalone artifacts.

layers.name: Reporting structure
layers.description: Post-to-post and agent reporting used to draw organization charts independently of incumbents.

findings.name: Reporting relationships
findings.description: ORG org:reportsTo holds between Agents or Posts and is the chart relationship. The Position Description also records supervisory relationships of the work. Matrix or dual reporting must be explicit.

questions.text: To which Position or Positions does this Position report, and is each link line, dotted, functional or matrix?
Which subordinate Positions report to this Position, and what span of control results?
Does this Position confer org:headOf or equivalent leadership of the host unit, independently of who occupies it?
When this Position is vacant, do reporting links remain on the Position so that the chart does not collapse onto the last occupant?

data_elements.name: Reports-to Position
data_elements.description: Position this Position reports to for org-chart purposes.

data_elements.name: Reporting type
data_elements.description: Line, functional, dotted or matrix qualification of a reports-to link.

data_elements.name: Head-of-organization flag
data_elements.description: Whether the Position is the formal head of the host organization or unit.

artifacts.name: Organization-chart fragment
artifacts.description: Serial snapshot of reporting links among Positions used to publish a chart independent of incumbents.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Chart-version identifier scoped to host organization plus observation timestamp; Position ids remain node keys.

layers.name: Abstract role binding
layers.description: Binding of the Position to a reusable function or role concept.

findings.name: Role or function of the post
findings.description: Popolo: many people fulfil the role CEO, but only one holds the post CEO at a named organization. ORG org:role on a Post indicates the role any holder plays. schema.org roleName is the occupancy-side analogue and must not replace the Post.

questions.text: What abstract role or function does any holder of this Position fulfil, and from which controlled vocabulary is it taken?
Is this organization using role-only memberships (for example club membership) for some relationships, and is this record still a true Position?
How is this Position’s role mapped to equivalent roles in other organizations for interoperability?

data_elements.name: Abstract role reference
data_elements.description: org:Role or equivalent SKOS concept the holder of the Position plays.

data_elements.name: Role label
data_elements.description: Lexical label of the function, used only when a Role resource is not yet minted.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Role bindings are references into a role or SKOS scheme owned outside this model.

bundles.name: Work content, authority and requirements
bundles.description: The duties, responsibilities, authorities and qualification requirements that constitute the work of the Position.
bundles.rationale: US statute defines a position as that work. The Position Description is the official record of duties, responsibilities and supervisory relationships and is the legal basis for appointment, pay, qualifications and performance planning. schema.org Occupation adds responsibilities, qualifications, skills and educationRequirements as occupation-level analogues.

layers.name: Duties and responsibilities
layers.description: Assigned work content of the Position.

findings.name: Assigned work content
findings.description: The Position is the work consisting of duties and responsibilities assigned by competent authority, whether or not an employee currently performs it. A PD is adequate when it contains enough information to determine title, series and grade.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of this Position and how does it relate to the host unit’s mission?
What major recurring duties and responsibilities are assigned, with what approximate percentage of time where recorded?
Which competent authority assigned these duties, and when was the assignment last certified as accurate?
Does one generic description cover a number of identical Positions, and if so which Position instances share it?

data_elements.name: Purpose statement
data_elements.description: Primary purpose of the Position in the host organization.

data_elements.name: Major duties
data_elements.description: Ordered collection of major regular and recurring duties.

data_elements.name: Generic description flag
data_elements.description: True when one official description covers multiple identical Position instances.

artifacts.name: Position description
artifacts.description: Official record of management’s assignment of duties, responsibilities and supervisory relationships, certified by the supervisor and classified by HR.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative PD number from the classification or HR office; version serial on each certified rewrite; Position master id as foreign key. A date is not the identifier.

layers.name: Authorities, qualifications and competencies
layers.description: What the holder is authorized to do and what the Position requires of any holder.

findings.name: Authorities and requirements of the Position
findings.description: FHIR records roles the practitioner is authorized to perform. schema.org Occupation records educationRequirements, qualifications, skills, experienceRequirements and responsibilities. Person-held licences remain outside this model; the Position stores the requirement.

questions.text: What decision, spending, hiring, clinical or signing authorities are attached to this Position rather than to a named person?
What education, licences, security eligibility, physical requirements and experience does this Position require of any holder?
Which competencies or skills are required or desired, from which competency framework, without copying the framework?
If a required credential expires, does that terminate occupancy (assignment) only, or does it also freeze the Position’s fill authority?

data_elements.name: Position authorities
data_elements.description: Authorizations that travel with the Position.

data_elements.name: Education requirements
data_elements.description: Educational background needed for the Position.

data_elements.name: Licence and credential requirements
data_elements.description: Required qualifications or credentials; the credentials themselves belong to the person.

data_elements.name: Competency requirements
data_elements.description: Referenced competencies with required proficiency.

artifacts.name: Qualification standard extract
artifacts.description: Cited extract or binding of the qualification standard used for this Position.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Qualification-standard identifier plus Position master id and effective interval.

bundles.name: Establishment, occupancy and lifecycle
bundles.description: Whether the Position is authorized, vacant, encumbered, frozen, abolished or otherwise in a lifecycle state, including rare multi-holder and unnamed-slot cases. Occupancy intervals belong to assignment.
bundles.rationale: ORG Posts may be unfilled. Popolo records creation and elimination dates and historical posts. FHIR allows an empty practitioner for unnamed roles and an active flag plus period. US law treats the Position as assignable work, not as the employee.

layers.name: Authorized establishment
layers.description: Budgeted or authorized capacity of the slot.

findings.name: Establishment and FTE capacity
findings.description: A Position is an established slot with authorized capacity. Full-time-equivalent fraction, headcount multiplicity and budget identity are Position-level, not person-level. ISO 30400 covers workforce planning and allocation vocabulary at family level; exact ISO term text for FTE was not inspectable here.

questions.text: Is this Position authorized on the establishment, and under which budget, complement or workforce-plan identity?
What full-time-equivalent capacity is authorized for this Position, and may it be job-shared across holders?
Is fill currently frozen, withheld or over-establishment, and by which authority?
When did authorized capacity last change, and what event (budget cycle, reorganization, reduction-in-force) caused it?

data_elements.name: Authorized flag
data_elements.description: Whether the Position is on the current establishment.

data_elements.name: Authorized FTE
data_elements.description: Authorized full-time-equivalent capacity of the slot.

data_elements.name: Maximum concurrent holders
data_elements.description: Upper bound on simultaneous occupants, covering job-share and ORG multi-holder posts.

data_elements.name: Freeze flag
data_elements.description: Whether recruitment or fill against the Position is currently withheld.

artifacts.name: Establishment authorization
artifacts.description: Instrument that created or last changed authorized capacity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authorization instrument identifier from the establishing authority; Position master id as foreign key.

layers.name: Vacancy and encumbrance
layers.description: Filled, vacant, acting-covered and unnamed-slot states without storing the person on the Position.

findings.name: Occupancy state of the slot
findings.description: ORG: a Post can exist without a holder; Membership does not exist without an Agent. Popolo: people hold posts through memberships; org:holds should not be used. FHIR: PractitionerRole.practitioner may be empty for an un-named surgeon-at-hospital slot; active and period describe the role record. Actual occupant and interval are WM-ORG-016.

questions.text: Is the Position currently vacant, encumbered, over-encumbered, or reserved, as derived from live assignments rather than a stored person field?
Which assignment records currently occupy this Position, including job-share fractions, and do they exceed authorized FTE?
Is this Position deliberately modelled with no practitioner or person (unnamed role at a location), and what services or locations still apply?
If someone is acting in this Position, is that an assignment overlay only, leaving the Position identity and classification unchanged?

data_elements.name: Occupancy state
data_elements.description: Derived code: vacant, encumbered, job-shared, over-encumbered, unnamed, reserved.

data_elements.name: Active flag
data_elements.description: Whether this Position record is in active use, analogous to FHIR PractitionerRole.active.

data_elements.name: Unnamed slot flag
data_elements.description: True when the Position is used without a named practitioner, as FHIR permits.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Occupancy state is derived from sibling assignment records plus Position capacity. Storing occupant identity on the Position would violate the Popolo and WM-ORG-016 boundary.

layers.name: Creation, change and abolition
layers.description: Lifecycle of the slot itself, distinct from occupant tenure.

findings.name: Position lifecycle events
findings.description: Popolo records date of creation and date of elimination of a post (for example an abolished electoral district). ORG ChangeEvent plus PROV-O describes substantial organizational change. Reclassification is a classification event on the same Position identity unless the work is so changed that a new Position is minted.

questions.text: When was this Position created or established, as event time versus the time that fact was observed or ingested?
When was the Position last reclassified or had its duties substantially redesigned, and did identity survive?
If abolished or eliminated, when did that take effect, may historical occupancy still be queried, and is the identifier retired rather than reused?
Which ORG or PROV change events link this Position to predecessor or successor Positions after merger, split or reorg?

data_elements.name: Valid from
data_elements.description: Creation or establishment instant of the Position, RFC 3339.

data_elements.name: Valid until
data_elements.description: Elimination or abolishment instant of the Position, RFC 3339.

data_elements.name: Lifecycle status
data_elements.description: draft, established, frozen, reclassified, abolished, superseded.

data_elements.name: Change event references
data_elements.description: ORG ChangeEvent or equivalent reorganization events affecting this Position.

artifacts.name: Establishment or abolishment notice
artifacts.description: Instrument that created, reclassified or eliminated the Position.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Instrument identifier from the establishing or abolishing authority plus event timestamp; Position master id remains the subject.

bundles.name: Location, time and working arrangement
bundles.description: Where and when the Position is based, including geographic jurisdiction, duty station and temporal validity of location facts.
bundles.rationale: ORG Sites attach to organizations; Popolo adds geographic area for constituency posts; FHIR Location is where the practitioner provides care; schema.org occupationLocation notes that requirements vary by jurisdiction.

layers.name: Duty station and site
layers.description: Physical or virtual place at which the Position’s work is performed.

findings.name: Position location
findings.description: Duty station, org:Site, FHIR Location and remote or hybrid arrangement of the slot, not of a particular occupant’s telework agreement.

questions.text: What is the official duty station or site of this Position, and is it a primary, registered or additional site?
Is remote, hybrid or multi-site work authorized for the Position itself, independent of an occupant’s personal agreement?
What contact details belong to the Post rather than to a named person, and when should they be unpublished because the post is vacant?
When did the duty station last change as an event, and when was that change observed?

data_elements.name: Site reference
data_elements.description: org:Site or equivalent place the Position is based at.

data_elements.name: Care location reference
data_elements.description: FHIR Location at which services of this role are provided.

data_elements.name: Work arrangement code
data_elements.description: On-site, hybrid, remote or roving arrangement authorized for the Position.

data_elements.name: Post contact details
data_elements.description: Contact means for the holder of the post as Popolo contact detail on Post.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Location and contact are references to site, address and contact-detail records; maps or floor plans belong to a place model.

layers.name: Geographic area and jurisdiction
layers.description: Constituency, coverage area and jurisdiction for which the Position is defined.

findings.name: Area and jurisdiction
findings.description: Popolo geographic area relates a post to a constituency or territory. schema.org occupationLocation is the region for which an occupational description is appropriate because requirements vary by jurisdiction.

questions.text: What geographic area, constituency or jurisdiction is this Position related to, and from which area register?
Which qualification or licence requirements of this Position are jurisdiction-specific?
Did elimination of an electoral or administrative area abolish this Position, as in the Popolo Annapolis example?

data_elements.name: Geographic area reference
data_elements.description: Area or constituency to which the post is related.

data_elements.name: Occupation location
data_elements.description: Region or country for which occupational requirements of this Position are stated.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Area references point at a geographic or jurisdiction model; geometry is not stored here.

bundles.name: Compensation, sensitivity and constraints
bundles.description: Position-level pay band, sensitivity and legal constraints, excluding occupant payroll.
bundles.rationale: ORG remuneration is a property of Role; schema.org estimatedSalary and EmployeeRole.baseSalary must not be collapsed. Statute excludes unpaid, fee-basis, seasonal and certain other work from GS classification. Sensitivity and privacy follow from whether a person is attached.

layers.name: Pay band, not person pay
layers.description: Remuneration range or salary band attached to the role or classified grade of the Position.

findings.name: Position remuneration band
findings.description: org:remuneration on Role, schema.org estimatedSalary on Occupation, and EmployeeRole.baseSalary on an employment relationship are different layers. This model stores only the Position or role band, with currency.

questions.text: What salary band, grade range or estimated salary distribution applies to this Position, in which currency, and is it binding or estimated?
Is the Position unpaid, nominal-pay, fee-basis, piece-work or otherwise outside ordinary classified pay, as 5 U.S.C. § 5102(c) enumerates?
Is actual occupant base salary stored only on the assignment or EmployeeRole, not on this Position?

data_elements.name: Pay band
data_elements.description: Minimum and maximum of the Position or role remuneration range.

data_elements.name: Currency code
data_elements.description: ISO 4217 currency for the band.

data_elements.name: Pay treatment code
data_elements.description: Classified, unpaid, fee-basis, piece-work, seasonal or other statutory treatment.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Pay-band figures are inline classified or estimated values. Binding pay tables live in a compensation register; occupant pay lives on assignment.

layers.name: Legal, sensitivity and privacy constraints
layers.description: Constraints on fill, disclosure and processing of Position records.

findings.name: Constraints on the Position
findings.description: Statutory exclusions from classification, sensitivity of filled-role records (FHIR Security Category Individual), and the rule that a vacant Position without a person is not personal data while occupancy is.

questions.text: Which statutory or policy regime applies to this Position, and is it excluded from the default classification or pay statute?
Does the current Position record contain personal data because occupancy, contact or named practitioner fields are populated, and what privacy basis applies?
What sensitivity, national-security or position-of-trust designation applies to the slot itself?
Who may read the Position Description versus occupant-identifying fields, and what exceptions exist for public official posts?

data_elements.name: Legal regime code
data_elements.description: Classification, labour or public-office regime covering the Position.

data_elements.name: Sensitivity code
data_elements.description: Position-of-trust or security-sensitivity designation of the slot.

data_elements.name: Contains personal data flag
data_elements.description: Whether the current record includes occupant-identifying or contact data.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Legal regime and sensitivity codes are inline constraints. Access-control policy documents belong to the Dimension service layer, not to each Position.

bundles.name: Governance, evidence, access and interoperability
bundles.description: Provenance, ownership, validation, retention, access and cross-standard profiles needed to operate the Position as a governed context model.
bundles.rationale: OPM requires supervisor certification of PD accuracy. ORG uses PROV-O for change. FHIR requires identifiers and active/period. Popolo and ORG profiles choose Post versus Membership. Retention of PD artifacts differs from retention of occupant personal data.

layers.name: Provenance, ownership and quality
layers.description: Who owns, certifies and quality-controls the Position record.

findings.name: Provenance and certification
findings.description: Immediate supervisor certifies PD accuracy; HR classifies. Change events should carry PROV attribution. Observation/ingestion time is recorded separately from event time.

questions.text: Which organization is the owner or joint owner of this Position record, and is it a bilateral record as the registry default implies?
Who certified the current Position Description and who classified it, at what event times?
Is the PD considered adequate for classification, outdated, under desk audit, or under appeal?
When was the current version ingested into the Dimension, as distinct from when the organizational event occurred?

data_elements.name: Owner organization
data_elements.description: Party accountable for the Position master record.

data_elements.name: Supervisor certifier
data_elements.description: Immediate supervisor who certified PD accuracy.

data_elements.name: Classifier
data_elements.description: HR or classification office that placed the Position in a class.

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when the Dimension observed or ingested this version.

artifacts.name: Certification cover sheet
artifacts.description: Signed or equivalently certified cover recording supervisor accuracy certification and HR classification, analogous to OF-08 or AD-332 practice.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Cover-sheet serial from the HR office plus Position master id and certification timestamp.

layers.name: Retention, access and exceptions
layers.description: How long Position artifacts are kept, who may access them, and which public-office exceptions apply.

findings.name: Retention and access rules
findings.description: Abolished posts remain queryable as historical structure. FHIR PractitionerRole is Individual security category when a practitioner is attached. Vacant public posts may still be published. Specific national retention schedules were not fetched in this run and remain a gap.

questions.text: How long is the Position Description and classification file retained after abolishment, and under which schedule?
Are occupant personal data and assignment records deleted or restricted on a different schedule from the Position slot?
Which fields of a public official’s Post are published, and which remain internal HR data?
What emergency, audit, or named-authority exceptions allow read of otherwise restricted Position or occupant fields?

data_elements.name: Retention schedule reference
data_elements.description: Cited records schedule for Position artifacts.

data_elements.name: Public disclosure flag
data_elements.description: Whether this Post is published as public structure.

data_elements.name: Security category
data_elements.description: FHIR-style security category or local analogue for the record as currently populated.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Retention and access rules are policy references on the Position. The schedules themselves are Dimension policy artifacts, not Position instances.

layers.name: Interoperability profiles
layers.description: Declared alignments and profile choices among ORG, Popolo, FHIR, schema.org, ISCO and local HR.

findings.name: Profile and alignment choices
findings.description: ORG says profiles may prefer Post or Membership. Popolo forbids org:holds and person-only holders. FHIR PractitionerRole is occupancy-leaning. schema.org Occupation is a profession. Conformance to any of these is claimed only when evidence of a chosen profile exists.

questions.text: Which interoperability profile is in force for this Position (ORG-Post-first, Popolo-membership-mediated, FHIR-role, local-HR), and where is it documented?
Which external identifiers or sameAs links assert equivalence to org:Post, Popolo Post, FHIR PractitionerRole or a local HRIS row, and are they same, close or related?
Which known conflicts (direct holds versus membership; Post as Organization; PractitionerRole as assignment) are unresolved for this instance?

data_elements.name: Interoperability profile
data_elements.description: Chosen profile governing occupancy and typing rules.

data_elements.name: Same-as links
data_elements.description: External identifiers and equivalence relations.

data_elements.name: Direct holds allowed
data_elements.description: Whether org:holds/heldBy may be materialized; Popolo says they should not.

artifacts.name: Interoperability profile declaration
artifacts.description: Documented choice of ORG, Popolo, FHIR or local-HR profile for this Dimension’s Position records.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Profile IRI or Dimension profile id plus version; not a Position instance id.

functions.name: Establish Position
functions.description: Create an authorized Position in a host organization with identity, title, capacity and initial lifecycle state, without requiring an occupant.
inputs: host organization and optional unit references
outputs: new Position record with master identifier
preconditions: Host organization exists and may contain Positions.
Establishing authority is competent to assign work.
No prohibited identifier collision with an active Position.
effects: Position exists independently of any person.
Organization chart may link the new Post.
Vacancy state is vacant unless an assignment is composed in the same transaction.

functions.name: Classify Position
functions.description: Analyse duties and responsibilities and place the Position in a class, series, title and grade or local job-evaluation outcome.
outputs: official title if the standard dictates one
preconditions: PD is certified accurate by the immediate supervisor.
Classifier is authorized under the applicable regime.
effects: Pay-band eligibility of the slot is set.
Occupant pay is not updated here; assignment compensation may need a follow-on process.

functions.name: Certify Position Description
functions.description: Record supervisor certification that the PD accurately describes assigned duties, responsibilities and supervisory relationships.
preconditions: Certifier is the immediate supervisor or delegated authority.
effects: PD becomes the official record for appointment, pay, qualifications, selection and performance planning.
Classification may now be performed or refreshed.

functions.name: Reclassify or redesign Position
functions.description: Apply a substantial change of duties or a new classification outcome, deciding whether identity survives or a successor Position is minted.
outputs: change event with event and observation times
effects: If identity survives, historical versions remain on the same master id.
If a new Position is minted, predecessor links are written and the old identifier is retired from active use.

functions.name: Abolish Position
functions.description: Eliminate a Position from the establishment while retaining historical query of the identifier.
preconditions: Position exists and is not already abolished.
Occupancy assignments are ended or transferred by WM-ORG-016 processes.
effects: Historical posts remain representable as in Popolo’s abolished-district example.
Identifier is not reused for a different work-slot.

functions.name: Evaluate occupancy state
functions.description: Derive vacant, encumbered, job-shared, over-encumbered or unnamed state from live assignments and authorized FTE without writing a person onto the Position.
inputs: authorized FTE and max concurrent holders
preconditions: Assignment records use this Position as their target.
Direct org:holds is not required and is forbidden under a Popolo profile.
effects: Position occupancy_state is a derived view.
Acting coverage does not mutate Position identity.

functions.name: Authorize fill or freeze
functions.description: Permit or withhold recruitment against a vacant Position, producing a fill-authorization that a JobPosting or requisition may reference.
preconditions: Position is established and not abolished.
Classification and PD are adequate if the local regime requires them before advertisement.
effects: A JobPosting may be linked as an advertisement of this vacancy; the posting is not the Position.
Freeze withholds fill without abolishing the slot.

functions.name: Align occupation and role
functions.description: Attach occupation-code and abstract-role mappings to the Position with explicit codebook and relation.
inputs: code set, code value and mapping relation
preconditions: Target codebook or role scheme is identified.
Mapping does not claim ISCO or ESCO conformance without evidence.
effects: Position becomes comparable across labour-market and civic vocabularies.
Occupation and Role masters remain outside this model.

composition.purpose: A unit instance contains or governs Positions via org:hasPost / org:postIn. The Position stores only the hosting link, not the unit tree.
A team is composed through Positions and assignments so that Positions remain reusable slots.
A Position is occupied through a scoped assignment or membership; occupant identity and interval are not stored as the Position.
Bind the organization-specific Position to a reusable function without owning the role taxonomy.
Align the Position’s job-slot to labour-market occupation codes with explicit codebook identity.
Duty station, org:Site or FHIR Location where the Position’s work is performed.
A vacancy advertisement may reference this Position; the posting is not the slot.
EmployeeRole is the occupancy-and-pay relationship; keep it off the Position except as an alignment of a composed assignment.
Healthcare role-at-organization-and-location, including unnamed empty-practitioner slots, aligned without claiming the FHIR resource is a classified HR Position.
ORG ChangeEvent builds on PROV-O for reorganization, derivation and attribution of Position change.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the owner organization, and any joint owner, accountable for Position master data and PD certification.
Bind the Position namespace to the host organization’s identifier register so that post numbers and IRIs cannot collide across employers.
Record the classification or HR office that is competent to assign class, title and grade where that regime applies.
Require every Position to name its interoperability profile (ORG-Post-first, Popolo-membership-mediated, FHIR-role, or local-HR).
dimension.namespace_guidance: Prefer the authoritative HRIS or public-organization position number as the master key; mint an HTTP IRI under the owner’s namespace for published Posts (pattern compatible with http://www.w3.org/ns/org#Post instances); assign a Dimension UUID or ULID only as a correlation key. Do not use titles, grades or dates as identifiers.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical identity is the master-system Position identifier; IRI and Dimension UUID are aliases.
Official title is stored separately from working title and from occupation label.
Occupancy state is derived from WM-ORG-016 assignments plus authorized FTE; person identifiers are not canonical fields of Position.
Timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z; event time and ingestion time are distinct fields.
Occupation and role codes always include codebook identity and version.
patch_rules: Patches to duties that affect classification must produce a new PD serial and may trigger reclassification.
Patches that only correct labels or contact details do not mint a new Position identity.
Occupancy changes patch assignments, not the Position, except for derived occupancy_state views.
Identifier reuse after abolishment is forbidden; successors are new ids with predecessor links.
compatibility_rules: An ORG-Post-first profile may materialize org:holds only as a derived view of assignments.
A Popolo profile must not persist org:holds or org:heldBy.
FHIR PractitionerRole mappings must state whether practitioner is required or the unnamed-slot pattern is in use.
Do not claim ISO 30400, ISCO, ORG or FHIR conformance unless a recorded profile and evidence support it.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier (HRIS position number, public-organization post id, classification PD number).
Governed global IRI for org:Post or Popolo Post when the Position is published.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension as a correlation key when the master system has none.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All event and observation timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; record organizational event time and Dimension ingestion/observation time separately.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts (PD, evaluation statement, establishment notice, chart fragment) use the master Position id plus a monotonic serial or version, not the title and not a bare date.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each serial artifact records a content hash or equivalent integrity stamp, certifier or classifier party, and the Position master id it describes.

policies: A Position may be created, classified, frozen, published and abolished without an occupant.
Occupant personal data, actual salary and tenure live on assignment records; access and retention of those fields follow privacy law, not the PD schedule.
Public official Posts may publish label, organization, area and vacancy while withholding HR evaluation content.
Reclassification, abolishment and fill-freeze are privileged operations with named competent authorities and audit.

read: Any agent with bundle-level read may see identity, official title, host organization, lifecycle status and public contact of a published Post.
PD narrative, evaluation factors, sensitivity and pay-band details require layer or finding scopes.
create: Only an establishing authority in the owner package may create a Position in a host unit.
Create must supply master id or request Dimension UUID minting, host organization, and official title.
update: Supervisor certification and HR classification are distinct update paths.
Derived occupancy_state is system-updated from assignments and is not directly writable.
Patches follow canon_and_patch rules for identity survival.
delete: Physical delete is not the default; abolish retires the identifier and retains historical query.
Hard delete of a Position is an exception requiring audit and only when legally compelled and no historical occupancy must be preserved.
Deletion of occupant PII does not delete the Position.

roles.name: Establishing authority
responsibilities: Authorize a new Position on the establishment.
Set initial FTE and host unit.

roles.name: Immediate supervisor
responsibilities: Assign duties, responsibilities and supervisory relationships.

roles.name: Classifier / HR office
responsibilities: Analyse work and assign class, series, title and grade or local equivalent.
Maintain evaluation statements and official titles.

roles.name: Position steward
responsibilities: Operate identifiers, interoperability profile and derived occupancy views.

roles.name: Audit and access officer
responsibilities: Grant exceptions to default read rules.
Ensure occupant PII is not leaked through Position publication.
Retain audit of classify, freeze, abolish and hard-delete operations.

access.default_rule: Default deny on evaluation content, sensitivity, pay-band internals and any occupant-derived fields; default allow on published identity, official title, host organization and lifecycle status of public Posts.
exceptions: Public-office transparency for elected or gazette Posts.
Named audit or legal-hold access to historical PDs.
Emergency fill against a vacant essential Position under recorded authority.
Unnamed FHIR-style clinical slots may expose service and location without a person.
audit_requirements: Record who classified, certified, froze, authorized fill, abolished or hard-deleted a Position, with event time and ingestion time.
Record access to occupant-derived views and to sensitivity-coded Positions.
Retain audit independently of occupant PII deletion.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.
Read the Specification URL for Position semantics and the chosen interoperability profile.
Read Processes URL for establish, classify, certify, occupy-via-assignment, freeze, abolish and audit paths.
Read Storage type URL and Interface URL only after the semantic contract is understood; JSON, YAML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections.

coverage.claim: This is a defensible wide-union context model of an organizational Position as an independent work-slot, grounded in W3C ORG Post, Popolo Post, US position-classification law and practice, ISCO-08 job/occupation definitions, schema.org Occupation/EmployeeRole and HL7 FHIR PractitionerRole. It is not a claim of universal coverage across military billets, academic lines, ISO 30400 quoted terms, or every national civil-service regime.

checklist.notes: Master-system id, IRI and Dimension UUID/ULID; titles are not identifiers; FHIR PractitionerRole.identifier and org:identifier included.
Establish, classify, reclassify, freeze, abolish, identity survival versus successor minting; Popolo creation and elimination dates.
Host organization/unit, reportsTo, role binding, ex officio, team compose, assignment compose.
RFC 3339 event versus ingestion time; validFrom/validUntil; FHIR period; occupancy intervals deferred to assignment.
Supervisor certification, classifier party, ORG ChangeEvent/PROV mix-in, artifact integrity.
Owner and joint-owner package, establishing authority, bilateral-record default from the registry context.
PD adequacy, classification status, profile constraints, identifier non-reuse, host-required rule.
Default deny on evaluation and occupant-derived fields; public Post publication; scoped bundle/layer/finding/artifact.
Abolish-with-history versus hard delete; separation of PD schedule from occupant PII; specific national schedules are a gap.
Explicit ORG versus Popolo versus FHIR versus schema.org profiles; ISCO/O*NET alignments; conflicts recorded rather than conformance claimed.
Class, series, grade, pay plan, supervisory determination and occupational code alignment.
Derived vacancy, job-share, unnamed slot, acting overlay; person not stored on Position.
Purpose, major duties, authorities, qualification and competency requirements.
Duty station, FHIR Location, Popolo area, jurisdiction-specific requirements.
Position/role pay band and statutory pay treatment; occupant salary excluded.

known_omissions: Full ISO 30400:2022 term entries for job, role, position and FTE were not inspectable; only the standard’s existence, date and chapter map were confirmed.
HR Open Standards / HR-XML Position and PositionOpening schemas were not retrieved as open full text.
Military billet versus rank, NATO manning, and academic faculty-line or endowed-chair semantics lack primary sources in this run and are gaps rather than canonical layers.
National archives retention schedules (for example NARA GRS) and GDPR storage-limitation periods are not cited as specific durations.
Dual-incumbency overlap windows for succession, career-ladder intern positions, and union-exclusivity of a slot are widely practised but not given primary support here.
Corporate statutory officer roles (director, company secretary) as Positions versus board membership remain unresolved against a possible sibling governance model.
ESCO occupation pillar beyond its ISCO mapping was not fetched.
conflicts: W3C ORG models occupancy as org:holds/heldBy on Post and treats Post as a subclass of Organization so a group may hold it; Popolo forbids org:holds/heldBy, requires occupancy through Membership, and restricts holders to persons.

HL7 FHIR PractitionerRole is primarily a period-bounded practitioner-at-organization-and-location record (assignment-shaped) that can also represent an unnamed slot; it is not equivalent to a classified HR Position or to org:Post.

ISCO ‘job’ (tasks of one person) and ‘occupation’ (set of similar jobs) are not the same as a US ‘position’ (work assignable to an employee) or a civic ‘post’ (organization-specific slot). schema.org Occupation is the profession kind; EmployeeRole is occupancy-and-pay.
schema.org Role.roleName / numberedPosition includes sports playing-position, which must not be imported as WM-ORG-004.
US GS class/grade/title rules are jurisdiction-specific; using them as if they were global would be a false conformance claim.
regional_assumptions: US Title 5 and OPM PD practice are used as a high-resolution public-service profile, not as a world default.
Popolo geographic-area and abolished-constituency examples are civic/legislative and may be unused in private-sector HR.
Ex officio Cabinet membership is a Westminster illustration in ORG; the pattern is reusable but the example is regional.
ISCO skill-level to ISCED-97 mapping is an ILO statistical convention and is not a hiring rule.
adversarial_checks: If a record cannot exist when vacant, it is an assignment or membership, not a Position.
If the only identifier is a person’s name, employee number or a start date, identity is wrongly sourced.
If CEO is modelled once globally rather than as CEO-at-organization, a Role has been stored as a Position.
If ISCO unit group is used as the Position id, an occupation has replaced the slot.
If a JobPosting is treated as the Position, a recruitment advertisement has replaced establishment.
If acting coverage rewrites official title or grade, occupancy has leaked into the slot.
If financial holdings, map coordinates or Quarterback are accepted as instances, the wrong sense of position has been admitted.
If org:holds is persisted under a Popolo profile, the declared interoperability profile is violated.
